question: Why did the integrated recovery route still show a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits?
question_long: Why did the integrated spent FCC catalyst recovery route still show a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits?
expect: premise false: after system expansion the net climate-change impact was negative, −2,257.14 kg CO2-eq per t (a net benefit) (abstract)
rendered: The integrated recovery route still showed a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits because the foreground climate-change impact of the leaching-residue-valorization stage was 1,940.11 kg CO2-eq, while the avoided-production credit was −2,922.21 kg CO2-eq, yielding a net stage result of −982.10 kg CO2-eq. However, the wet-recovery stage still had a net climate-change impact of −1,275.04 kg CO2-eq. Therefore, the overall net climate-change impact of the integrated recovery route was still positive (−982.10 - 1,275.04 = - 2,257.14 kg CO2-eq), but negative.
